en: The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Mantra for Expelling Thieves and Harm.
Homage to the Buddha. Homage to the Dharma. Homage to the Sangha of Bhikṣus. Homage to the Seven Buddhas of the Past.
Homage to all Buddhas. Homage to the disciples of all Buddhas. Homage to all teachers. Homage to all...
The Master and his disciples paid homage to the Ghost King Mūliśrī and,
having performed this salutation, spoke this mantra.
May all my incantations be fulfilled according to my wishes.
To the north there is a mountain named Gandhamādana,
where a king of the ghost spirits named Mūliṅga resides.
There are four sisters. What are these four? Āndhanī, Yamani, Śamani, and Anaghani.

Āndhanī makes the eyes of the thieves blind; Anaghani causes the thieves to stand still; Śamani causes the thieves to sit down; Anaghani causes the thieves to become deluded. When they are thus deluded—Ulūlī, Mūlī, Dantidhā, Padumā, Cakalī—they shall cause the mouths and teeth of the thieves to clench, until the threads are loosened, at which point they may be released. Having spoken this incantation:
He then says: "For the sake of such-and-such persons, I shall provide protection and ward off evil spirits and harms, causing them all to attain peace and security.
This is said at the very beginning when one recites this sutra.
On the twenty-ninth day of the month,
one should light seven lamps before the Buddha, burn resin incense,
scatter flowers, and recite the mantra.
Recite this mantra seven times and offer prayers for the King of Ghosts, Murala, so that he may attain merit and virtue;
likewise, light lamps, burn incense, and scatter flowers. Furthermore, light seven lamps, burn incense, and scatter flowers for Hārītī, the Mother of Ghosts.
When this sutra has been recited seven times, the mantra will then grant its response accordingly. Thus it is said:
"It shall be as you wish."
The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī for Expelling Thieves and Harm Spoken by the Buddha.
